welcome.script:
Hi, scientists! Welcome to the Field Station. Today you're not just reading about science. You're solving a real mystery.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach · CAM 2 woods · CAM 3 river · CAM 4 marsh]
Look at these four pictures. They came from trail cameras along the Florida coast. A baby sea turtle. A panther. A manatee. A cottonmouth snake. What do you notice?

[ON SCREEN: The times]
Now look at the little clock on each camera. 9:14. 9:14. 9:15. 9:15. All four animals moved within about two minutes! And the cameras were far apart, so the animals couldn't see or hear each other. Hmm. I wonder why.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
That's our case: what made four animals react at almost the same time, and how did each one know?

[ON SCREEN: Your clue bar]
Here's how you'll solve it. See the bar right under the tabs that says "My clues"? It has four question marks. Every time you finish one of the games in this lesson, a question mark turns into a clue. When you have all four, you'll crack the case at the top of the Assignment.

One more thing: tap your first name into the Field Station ID card so the clues are saved as yours. And if you like taking pictures, try the Photo Hunt. It's optional, but it's fun.

Now press Listen on Dr. Reyes's walkie-talkie, right below me. She's the scientist who set up these cameras.

warmup.script:
Before we look at any animals, let's start with you, because your body does this too.

[ON SCREEN: The snap test]
Under Dr. Reyes's walkie-talkie there's a game called "Hear the snap." Tap the trail picture to start. Then wait. Don't guess! When you hear the snap, or see the trail flash gold, tap as fast as you can. Do it three times. I'll try it right now.

(Do the test once on camera. Read your time out loud.)

Whoa. I didn't stop and think, "I should tap now." My body just did it.

[ON SCREEN: Your steps]
Then, in the boxes below the game, write what happened in your body, in order. Start with the sound and end with your tap or your turn. Try for at least three steps. There's no wrong answer yet. We'll check your steps later today.

Wonder about this: how did your body decide that fast? Press Listen and hear what Dr. Reyes thinks.

vocab.script:
These are the six words you'll use all lesson. Four of them are the steps you're about to learn, so let's act them out together. Stand up if you can!

[ON SCREEN: Stimulus]
Stimulus. Something happens in the world. (Snap your fingers.)

[ON SCREEN: Sense organ]
Sense organ. A body part picks it up. (Point to your ear.)

[ON SCREEN: Brain]
Brain. It decides what that means. (Tap your head.)

[ON SCREEN: Response]
Response. You do something. (Turn around.)

[ON SCREEN: Act it out]
Again, faster: snap, ear, head, turn! Hey, that's exactly what happened in your snap test.

[ON SCREEN: Word Lens]
Now look below me at the Word Lens. Tap each colorful word sticker. Dr. Reyes looks at it through her binoculars and reads you the word and what it means. When all six stickers have a green check, you're ready for the lesson.

lesson.script:
[ON SCREEN: This tab]
Welcome to the lesson tab. It has three parts, and two of your clues are hiding here.

Part 1 teaches the four steps, and then you'll play Send the Signal. That's clue two. Part 2 is about different senses. There's an alligator picture and a raccoon question. Part 3 is the big one: you'll open Dr. Reyes's four trail cameras. That's clue three.

Go in order, and keep an eye on your clue bar at the top. Let's start with Part 1.

part1.label: Part 1 · the four steps + Send the Signal

parts.label: 🔁 The four steps
parts.title: Every animal reaction

A body part picks it up: eyes, ears, nose, tongue or skin.
The brain decides what it means.

parts.label: 📡 Send the signal

Start where the message starts: out in the world.
Fill all four and watch the signal run. That’s Clue 2!

part1.script:
Remember your snap test? Let's put names on what happened.

[ON SCREEN: The four steps]
Every time an animal reacts, the same four steps happen, in order. One: a stimulus. Something happens, like the snap. Two: a sense organ picks it up. For the snap, that was your ears. Three: your brain decides what it means. "Something's behind me!" Four: the response. You turned around, or you tapped.

Here's something amazing: all four steps can happen in less than one second.

Now look at your warm-up list. Did you write a step for your brain? Lots of people skip it, because it happens so fast you can't feel it.

[ON SCREEN: Send the signal]
After you read Part 1, scroll down to the game called Send the Signal. Drag each step onto a station in order, starting out in the world. When all four are right, you'll watch the signal run. That's clue two!

First, press Listen. Dr. Reyes has something to tell you about the middle steps.

part2.label: Part 2 · different senses

parts.label: 👀 Five senses
parts.title: Each sense organ picks up something different
rows: touch, heat and cold, and pain

parts.label: ⚠ Watch out
parts.title: The brain can’t do it alone
parts.body: No sense organ, no signal. No signal, no response.

part2.script:
Animals don't all notice the same things. A bald eagle spots a fish from way up in the sky with its eyes. A panther hears a tiny rustle in the leaves.

[ON SCREEN: Five senses]
Each sense organ picks up a different kind of information. Eyes pick up light. Ears pick up sound. Your nose, smell. Your tongue, taste. And your skin picks up touch, heat and cold.

[ON SCREEN: Watch out]
Watch out for a common mistake. Some people think the brain does all the work. But the brain can't notice anything by itself! A sense organ has to pick it up first. No sense organ, no signal. No signal, no response. Keep that in mind. It will help you at the very end of the assignment.

figure.label: The alligator picture + the raccoon

parts.label: 🦝 The raccoon
parts.title: Fill in the four boxes
parts.body: A raccoon freezes when it hears a barking dog. Type one short answer in each box: stimulus, sense organ, brain, response.

figure.script:
[ON SCREEN: Alligator pathway]
Let's read this picture together, left to right, like a sentence.

[ON SCREEN: Read it left to right]
First, a splash in the water. That's the stimulus. The alligator's ear picks it up: the sense organ. A signal zips to its brain, and the brain decides, "Food might be over there!" Then the alligator turns toward the splash. That's the response.

What do you notice about the yellow lines? They show the message traveling.

[ON SCREEN: The raccoon]
Right under the picture is a Stop and Reason question with four boxes. A raccoon freezes when it hears a barking dog. Type one short answer in each box. Here's a hint for the brain box: what do you think the raccoon decided? Your answers are saved for you at the end of the lesson.

part3.script:
Now it's time to look at the evidence, just like a real field scientist.

[ON SCREEN: How to open a camera]
Below Dr. Reyes's walkie-talkie are her four trail cameras. Tap one to open it. Then press Next step, and you'll follow the message through that animal one step at a time: stimulus, sense organ, brain, response.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach]
As you open each one, ask yourself one question: what started this animal's reaction? Was it the same thing for all four? Or something different? That's how you'll earn clue three.

[ON SCREEN: The manatee photo]
After the cameras, there's a real photo of a Florida manatee. Tap each number on the photo to see what it uses to feel the water. Then match the steps.

[ON SCREEN: Sealed field fact]
And don't skip the sealed field fact at the bottom. Tap it to crack it open. It's about baby sea turtles, and it's one of my favorite facts.

Now press Listen. Dr. Reyes will tell you what to watch for.

explore.label: Explore · the heron on CAM 5 (Clue 4)

parts.label: 📖 The heron story
parts.title: A heron hunting
parts.body: A great blue heron stands still in shallow water. A small fish swims into view. The heron freezes, then strikes. Its sharp beak grabs the fish.

parts.label: 🃏 One card, sorted
parts.title: A small fish swims into view.
rows: It happens out in the water, before the heron does anything. It starts everything.

parts.label: 🧠 The hidden step
parts.title: No camera can see it

Tool of the Week: the trail camera!

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: The heron]
This is CAM 5. It caught a great blue heron hunting, just one minute after the other four cameras.

[ON SCREEN: The heron story]
Read the heron story first, slowly. A heron stands still in the water. A small fish swims into view. The heron freezes, then strikes, and grabs the fish. What do you notice? I notice it froze first. I wonder why?

[ON SCREEN: One card, sorted]
In the sorting game, drag each card into its step. Let me do one with you. "A small fish swims into view." Is that something happening in the world, a body part, or something the heron did? It happens out in the water before the heron does anything. So it's the stimulus! You sort the rest.

[ON SCREEN: The hidden step]
Notice the pink box: the brain. You can't drop a card there, because no camera can film what happens inside the heron's head. You'll explain that step yourself in Step 3, lower on this tab.

[ON SCREEN: Then]
After the sort, find the four steps on a real heron photo, and answer Steps 1 to 4 right in the boxes. And if you finish early, open the Tool of the Week at the bottom. It's a trail camera, and it has a sense organ too!

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has one more thing to say about the heron.

quiz.script:
[ON SCREEN: Self-Check]
This Self-Check is not graded. It's just for you, to see what stuck.

You'll get one question at a time. Pick an answer, and then press Next question. If you pick a wrong answer, don't worry. Read the hint that pops up. It tells you what to think about. Take a breath, think about the four steps, and give it a try.

assignment.script:
You made it to the assignment! This is where you show what you know.

[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
First, crack the case. If the case is still locked, you're missing a clue. Tap "Show me where the clues are," then tap "Go there" to jump right to it. When you have all four clues, read the three answers and pick the one that fits every clue. Think about the cameras: did all four animals react to the same thing?

[ON SCREEN: Today’s parts]
Then there are four parts. Part A: drag each step word into its blank. Part B: answer three questions in complete sentences. Part C: make up your own Florida animal moment and sketch it. And last, a CER. I'll help you with each part as you get there.

[ON SCREEN: Saved for you]
Everything you type saves itself and shows up in Gathered Answers at the bottom of this tab. That's what you turn in.

Now press Listen. Dr. Reyes wants this to read like a real field report.

partb.script:
[ON SCREEN: Part B tools]
Part B has three questions. Answer each one in complete sentences, using our step words.

Under each box you'll see "Your answer needs." Those little chips light up green as you include each part. That's how you know you've got everything. Stuck? Press "Need a hint?" It gives one hint at a time. And if you highlighted something earlier, "My evidence" lets you add it to your answer.

[ON SCREEN: CAM 1 beach · CAM 2 woods]
For question five, you'll pick one animal from last night's cameras. The four cameras are right there above the question, so you don't have to go back.

partc.script:
Now it's your turn to be the scientist.

[ON SCREEN: Your scenario]
In Part C, you'll make up a short moment, like the heron story, about a Florida animal that wasn't in today's lesson. Maybe a pelican, a bobcat, an anole lizard, or a dolphin. Fill in the four boxes: what happened, what body part noticed it, what the brain decided, and what the animal did.

[ON SCREEN: The sketch pad]
Then sketch it. Draw with the pen. To add a label, choose the Label tool, drag from a part of your drawing to an empty spot, and type its name. A line will point right to it. Add arrows to show the order of the steps. Take your time. Real scientists sketch what they observe all the time.

parts.label: 💬 The classmate says

parts.body: “Animals just react. They don’t really need a brain. Their senses do all the work.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

parts.label: 🧩 The planner

rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.
They drop into your C and E boxes. You write the R.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The classmate says]
A classmate says, "Animals just react. They don't really need a brain. Their senses do all the work." Hmm. Think back to Part 2 and the hidden pink box from the heron. Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Remember CER. Your claim is what you think is true. Your evidence is facts from today's lesson. Your reasoning explains how those facts prove your claim.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Use the planner first. Tap "I agree" or "I disagree." Then tap two pieces of evidence. Watch them drop right into your Claim and Evidence boxes! The reasoning box is all you. Explain why your evidence proves your claim. Try starting with "This shows that…"

closing.script:
[ON SCREEN: Case closed · Confetti]
Case closed! You did it, scientists.

So what really happened that night? Four animals, four different things they noticed, and four different senses. And each animal's own brain decided what to do. One loud noise didn't explain it. The four steps did.

[ON SCREEN: Before you go]
Before you go, three last things. Answer the Big Question in two or three sentences, using at least three of our step words. Check off each box in What to Turn In. When they're all checked, you'll collect a heron feather for your Field Notebook. And download your field journal. It has your answers, your sketch and your photos.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Now press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a sneak peek at what's coming next time.
